mechanisms.behavior: The proven table creates four balls and initializes switches 18-21 active. Output 1 ejects the ball at switch 21 into the shooter path; switch 22 is the downstream jam opto.
mechanisms.label: Four-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 launches a ball held at shooter-lane switch 23; the proven script uses power 55.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 51 stays active while a ball is held. Output 6 ejects at approximately 39.5 degrees with strength 54 in the proven table.
mechanisms.label: Right eject scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Output 20 moves the grave marker between its down switch 33 and up switch 34. Output 3 controls the ball magnet and switch 52 senses the captured ball. Output 19 is the marker's primary visual flasher.
mechanisms.label: Motorized grave marker and magnet

mechanisms.behavior: Output 4 holds a ball at electric-chair opto 53. Output 18 drives the Sparky head/step-up animation; standup switch 35 reports a direct hit.
mechanisms.label: Electric Chair and Sparky step-up

mechanisms.behavior: Output 53 swings the hammer through its unsensed stroke. Impacts on the captive-ball assembly pulse switch 42; the mechanism has no controller-facing hammer-position sensor.
mechanisms.label: Hammer and captive ball

mechanisms.behavior: The three targets begin raised. Ball impact drops targets and asserts switches 60-62; output 54 raises the complete bank.
mechanisms.label: Three-bank drop targets

mechanisms.behavior: Output 55 raises the loop post while enabled and releases it when disabled. The official auxiliary-board table and proven VPW callback agree; there is no controller-facing position switch.
mechanisms.label: Loop up post

mechanisms.behavior: Coffin optos 57-59 track the bottom, middle, and top lock positions. Output 51 retracts the lock post to release stored balls.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball coffin lock

mechanisms.behavior: Output 52 lowers the magnet and asserts position switch 64. Processor outputs 57/58 are D0/D1: 00 is off, 10 is detect/hold for up to 10 seconds, 11 is detect with a 250 ms cadence, and 01 is a full-power centered grab for up to 1 second. Detection is reported on switch 63 only in detect/hold or detect mode.
mechanisms.label: Coffin magnet processor

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 54 holds the snake ball and output 5 ejects it. Output 12 releases the jaw latch and the proven script reports jaw-open switch 55; output 56 closes the jaw, with switch 56 pulsing at the latch contact.
mechanisms.label: Snake jaw, latch, and eject

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 15/16 drive the left/right flippers from buttons 84/82 with normally-closed EOS contacts 83/81.
mechanisms.label: Two lower flippers

The official red-GI map proves nine wedge-base and two bayonet fixtures. The exact table exposes ten one-for-one GIR authoring-light centers; the eleventh physical socket remains proven by the manual but is not assigned a fabricated point. Recreate all 11 from the manual map and treat these ten coordinates as calibrated anchors.
The official blue-GI map proves nine wedge-base and two bayonet fixtures, matching the exact table's 11 GIB centers.

Driver-board CN22 feeds five front spot lamps and six back-panel lamps. The five exact GIWU spot centers are in playfield space; the manual-proven six back-panel fixtures remain in the quantity but intentionally have no playfield coordinate.

Driver-board CN23 feeds the white LED system. The manual proves 22 wedge-base and two bayonet playfield fixtures plus two wedge-base and two bayonet bottom-arch fixtures. The exact table exposes 22 GIW authoring centers; the remaining six physical sockets stay explicit in quantity and in the manual map rather than receiving invented separation coordinates.
This is PinMAME's aggregate compatibility callback, not another physical GI circuit. Physical emitters are represented only by public lamp channels 130, 132, 134, and 136.
